title: What to make, and what it meets

blocks.text: Eleven things you can ask for and six of them are not living artefacts. Your skills mostly stack on top of this runtime rather than compete with it; two genuinely collide, and one of those is the likeliest source of the next mess. Pin a note on any row.

blocks.title: Three words used on this page
blocks.text:
The **model** is the document's content as data: a list of blocks with stable ids. It is the truth.
The **page** is what you are reading: a rendering of the model. Editing the page edits the model; the page is never read back.
A **template** is one of three read-mode layouts the model can be drawn in. `house` is the default, a tabbed spec. `desk-research` is one long page for analysis. `brief` is a one-pager, which is what this page uses.

blocks.info: The question that picks the row is what the thing is for, never what it looks like.

blocks.title: The Publish button: two of your three outputs work
blocks.text:
**A static read-only HTML, the same as Preview.** Possible today, two ways. `build.mjs export` already writes one into the document's folder from the model. The button itself can hand you the file through the download prompt, but it cannot choose the folder: a page cannot write to your disk, only offer a file.

**Its own Claude artefact holding that static copy.** Not possible from the button. A page can republish itself and nothing else; the capability has no target other than the artefact it belongs to. What works instead: the button writes the static HTML into this document's own store, and I publish or update the companion artefact from there in a session. One click from you, one step from me, and the static artefact keeps its URL across updates.

**Updating this artefact.** Already happens on every save: a new immutable version, same URL, version picker.

blocks.info: D-1 is settled. Two left, and neither blocks the Publish button.
